takeaways.label: H1 revenue up ~30% YoY, profitability ahead of revenue
takeaways.text: Finished goods volume grew 24% and realizations improved ~5% to Rs.260 per kg, while EBITDA per kg improved despite raw material and freight cost pressures.

takeaways.label: Order book and capacity build signal doubling ambition
takeaways.text: A Rs.300 cr data center order (through 2033), Rs.95 cr of Asian export orders, and a new Rs.500 cr capex plan underpin management's visibility of current sales doubling in 3–4 years.

takeaways.label: Machining mix and realizations climbing
takeaways.text: Machining contribution reached 90% in H1 (vs 88% last year), Q2 realizations hit Rs.267 per kg, and absolute EBITDA per kg improved sequentially despite cost headwinds.

takeaways.label: Export freight and cost pass-through created a temporary drag
takeaways.text: Ocean freight nearly doubled selling costs on exports last quarter, and while 80% of domestic cost increases have been passed through, not all export costs have been recovered yet.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Recognition of in-transit North American PV sales, the pace of new order closures toward the Rs.500 cr target, and whether the heavy hammer line cold trials begin on schedule in January/February.

points.label: Commercial vehicle
points.text: High-teen H1 growth, with domestic business growing in the mid-20s, broadly in line with MHCV production and sales growth in India; exports remained subdued due to longer shipment times and higher sales in transit.

points.label: Farm equipment
points.text: Over 20% H1 growth; domestic business registered high-teen growth, outperforming domestic tractor production and sales growth; market share gained from 42% to almost 46% this year, with all lines fully ramped up despite an overall market that was down.

points.label: Industrial segment
points.text: Growth well above 50% in H1, supported by strong traction in both domestic and export markets; recent order wins in crankshaft businesses for Japanese and Asian markets.

points.label: Off-highway
points.text: Over 50% H1 growth, with both domestic and export markets contributing; domestic construction equipment saw healthy growth supported by project awards in road, highways, and infrastructure.

points.label: Passenger vehicle
points.text: Revenue almost doubled YoY in H1; domestic growth supported by healthy market demand and increased wallet share; two new domestic PV programs entered, starting in Q4 and Q2 of next financial year.

points.label: North American exports
points.text: PV programs and industrial programs (small portable gensets) going well; a 4,000-ton press line commissioned for a North American PV client, with a large part of Q2 sales in transit on DAP basis, to be recognized from Q3.

quotes.text: Ashish Garg: "We have been able to sustain profitability levels at or above those achieved in FY2026, despite an increase in raw material prices and other cost pressures. This has enabled us to deliver profitability growth ahead of revenue growth, reflecting the strength of our diversified business portfolio, increasing value addition, and our continued focus on operational excellence."

points.label: Ultra-heavy component facility (Rs.650 cr)
points.text: Expected to complete and commence operation in Q4 FY28, with a 20 MW captive solar power plant; balance capex of ~Rs.50 cr this year and ~Rs.250 cr next year.

points.label: New Rs.500 cr capex
points.text: Board-approved, to be funded through a combination of debt and internal accruals, implemented in phases across FY28 and FY29; 70% machining, 30% forging (small press lines), driven by demand for gensets, CV exports, and PV requirements.

points.label: Heavy hammer line
points.text: Equipment already arrived; cold trials expected in January/February, hot trials by March; sample submissions in FY2028, with revenues factored in only from Q3 and Q4 FY2028.

points.label: Vertical upsetter line
points.text: Developmental activities already started; the line is already booked with Rs.150 cr of orders.

points.label: Machining capacity
points.text: Utilization already peaked at 80% last quarter, expected to hit ~90% by Q4, driven by strong order books and ongoing program development; lead time for adding machining capacity is nearly one year.

points.label: Total capacity post-expansion
points.text: Combined investments to add 59,000 metric tons forging and 34,000 tons machining capacity, leading to total ~2,17,000 tons forging and 1,16,000 tons machining in the next 2–2.5 years.

points.label: Solar project
points.text: First ground-mounted 33 MW solar project, 90% capex done; some generation expected in Q4, full generation by Q1 next year; expected to add almost 1.5% to EBITDA, with ~Rs.30 cr in annual power savings.

quotes.text: Ashish Garg: "If we are investing and we are able to utilize those assets, is the best-case scenario that probably can happen in our industry."

points.label: Data center order
points.text: Rs.300 cr per annum secured roughly through 2033; the customer has also invested in plants; management noted this represents only ~5% of the total market size, implying significant headroom.

points.label: Export order wins
points.text: Gained almost Rs.95 cr of export orders in the last quarter for the Asian region; ~Rs.80 cr of business secured for new global development for one large North American engine manufacturer, currently in trial/testing phase, which is for the North American CV programs.

points.label: Fungible forging line
points.text: Management aims to close nearly Rs.500 cr of new orders (out of ~Rs.1,000 cr in discussions) by this financial year, pending capability demonstration; by March, orders of close to Rs.500 cr expected on this line.

points.label: Beyond data centers
points.text: The heavy forging line is fungible across gas engine products, oil and gas, railways, defense, and wind applications (anything beyond 300 kg); the existing 19L–60L engine family business (Rs.500 cr–Rs.600 cr) is also growing due to energy needs.

points.label: European CV opportunity
points.text: RFQ processes started from a domestic customer's acquisition; business award likely in 2–3 years, a medium-term opportunity.

quotes.text: Ashish Garg: "It's not only products related to data center application. The shafts that we are working on, we are also working on the energy needs right now. Energy requirements are going up. So there are gas engine products are also there. There are oil and gas products which are also there, and there are wind sector products which are there. It's a fungible line."

points.label: Margin stability
points.text: Gross, EBITDA, and PAT margins remained healthy and broadly stable YoY in Q2, with only a sequential moderation, despite raw material price increases and higher shipment costs.

points.label: EBITDA per kg improved
points.text: Absolute EBITDA per kg improved despite all cost pressures, indicating competitive positioning; management expects this to be maintained in H2, and to continue improving even if raw material prices go beyond a certain range.

points.label: Cost pass-through
points.text: On the domestic side, almost 80% of OEMs have paid off cost increases; 80% of total cost increases have been passed through overall; raw material is a complete pass-through.

points.label: Export freight headwind
points.text: Ocean freights were at peak last quarter, causing selling costs on exports to nearly double; not everything has been paid off yet, though freight is now softening.

points.label: ROCE
points.text: 19.6% including CWIP; ~25% excluding CWIP assets in the quarter.

quotes.text: Ashish Garg: "The absolute EBITDA per kg, despite the cost pressures, have improved, if you see, which is an important point to be seen. That is how we see, despite all the pressures, the EBITDA per kg has improved. Going forward, we see that it will be kind of maintained in H2 as well. If raw material prices go beyond a certain range, probably, but EBITDA per kg for us will still continue to improve."

points.label: Operating cash flow
points.text: H1 FY27 at ~Rs.124 crores, temporarily impacted by working capital investment (higher receivables aligned with top-line expansion) and Rs.35 crores in strategic advance payments to raw material suppliers; normalization expected over the full year, yielding significantly stronger cash flow conversion.

points.label: Balance sheet strength
points.text: Total outside liability to net worth at 0.21x; net debt to equity at 0.08x; cash and liquid reserves of ~Rs.350 crores provide strong buffer for capex with minimal reliance on external borrowings.

points.label: Debt for new capex
points.text: Rs.300 cr debt sanction for the new Rs.500 cr capex; actual utilization may be lower; year-end balance sheet liquidity expected to remain strong, and by end of next financial year, numbers will look very similar to current levels.

points.label: Capex intensity rising
points.text: Management noted capex intensity will be bigger than the last 3 years, adding Rs.500 cr of top line in one year and Rs.150 cr of EBITDA.

items.title: Heavy forging entry (Dugri)
items.text: A ₹650 cr programme (₹300 cr already spent) is building one of the world's largest hammer lines (~2,000 tonnes/month) for 300 kg-3 ton components, with ~₹300 cr/year of data-center orders secured, visibility to 2033, and ~₹500 cr more targeted to close in FY27. Revenues start Q3-Q4 FY28 and the line can do ₹1,600-1,800 cr/year at ₹800/kg machined realisations - the single biggest earnings step-up in the pipeline.

items.title: ₹950 cr new-business order book
items.text: The order book of peak incremental annual revenue, executable over FY27-FY29 with 80-85% delivered by FY28, carries realisations of ₹340-350/kg versus the current ₹240-245/kg. The ~₹95/kg mix uplift flows straight into gross margin, and exports (~50% of the book, H1 FY27 up 36% YoY) add a second growth engine.

items.title: ₹500 cr machining-led capex
items.text: On 5 November 2026 the Board approved ₹500 cr across FY28-FY29, ~70% machining and 30% forging where small press lines are at peak utilization. Together with the heavy programme it takes capacity to ~2,17,000 MT forging and 116,000 MT machining, and management expects ~₹150 cr of EBITDA from a single year's ₹500 cr spend.

items.title: Passenger vehicle ramp-up
items.text: PV has grown from 4% of FY25 revenue to 9% of H1 FY27, with the 4,000-ton press line for a North American client recognising revenue from Q3 FY27 and ₹80-100 cr of sales projected from that facility alone. Two new domestic programs start in Q4 and Q2 of next financial year, and management targets 12-15% of revenues in three to four years.

items.title: Captive solar power (Muktsar)
items.text: The ~33 MW captive solar plant is ~90% built, starts Q4 FY27 with full generation from Q1 FY28. It cuts power cost by almost ₹30 cr a year, adding ~1.5% to EBITDA and supporting margins above 30%.

items.title: Domestic share gains in farm and CV
items.text: Farm equipment share has risen to ~46% with all lines fully ramped, and CV share is expected to move from 32% to 42% on the MHCV side with CV revenue growing 35-40% this year on new programs. Share gains on an already-installed base convert to revenue without fresh capex.
